You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

Based on the chest X-ray findings, which of the following best describes the observed pathology in the right upper lobe, and what is the most likely diagnosis? 

A) A well-defined mass with calcification in the right upper lobe bronchus causing atelectasis, suggestive of a calcified granuloma.
B) An elliptical enhancing mass in the right upper lobe bronchus with associated patchy consolidation, suggestive of a bronchial carcinoid.
C) A spherical mass in the right upper lobe with diffuse consolidation, indicative of a primary lung carcinoma.
D) A poorly defined mass in the right upper lobe with no associated consolidation, consistent with a benign pulmonary nodule.
E) A peripherally located mass with pleural effusion in the right upper lobe, suggestive of metastatic disease.
F) A mass in the right upper lobe with cavitation, indicative of a necrotic infectious process.
